claims.explanation: Nobiletin is annotated as a MEK inhibitor and its transcriptional response most closely resembles the MEK inhibitor U-0126, suggesting that selectivity is driven by MAPK pathway dependency. Lines with MAP2K1 mutation or upstream RTK/RAS/BRAF activation (e.g., EGFR, BRAF, KRAS, NF1) are more sensitive, while lines with PIK3CA/PTEN alterations or a mesenchymal/osteosarcoma-like state are relatively protected.

features.basis: Drug annotated as MEK inhibitor; MAP2K1-mutant NCIH1437 is among the most killed lines
BRAF-mutant melanoma/colorectal/endometrial lines are enriched among sensitive lines
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (NCIH1650, HCC4006, NCIH1648) are among the most killed
KRAS-mutant pancreatic/ovarian lines are enriched among sensitive lines
NF1 loss activates RAS-MAPK and several NF1-mutant lines are sensitive
PTEN-mutant lines are enriched among the least affected lines
PIK3CA-mutant lines are enriched among the least affected lines
Higher MAP2K1 expression may increase dependence on MEK signaling
Higher BRAF expression may increase MAPK pathway output and MEK dependence
Higher KRAS expression may increase MAPK pathway output and MEK dependence
Higher EGFR expression may increase upstream MAPK signaling and MEK dependence
Lower PTEN expression may shift dependence away from MAPK toward PI3K-AKT
